- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% bias to early periods.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting; delay correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual downward slope.
- Mean reversion is often overestimated; if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend unless sentiment strongly diverges.
